transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-03-15 14:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Zoom / Fireflies capture
Attendees: Maya Spencer (Redwood AE), Carlos Nguyen (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Redwood CSM); Tom Reyes (BlueMarble VP Eng), Lin Zhao (BlueMarble SRE Lead), Amira Hassan (BlueMarble Head of Product)

Summary:
Brief debrief after the weekend surge that triggered our auto-throttle and caused ~15–20% request rejections at peak for 11:45–12:30 PST. Focus was on root cause hypotheses (burst vs long-tail KV cache misses vs router saturation), mitigations (dedicated pool vs conservative throttle), and a concrete test/bench plan. Customer requested actionable next steps and logs to validate whether Dedicated or a config change is best.

Topics (auto sections may be imperfect):
- Incident timeline and observed symptoms
- Hypotheses: KV cache coldness, request burst pattern, router saturation, model context length spikes
- Proposed mitigations: short-term routing fallback, prefix cache warmers, dedicated pool sizing, throttling smoothing
- Ops plan: bench tests, logs to collect, roll-forward policy, stakeholder signoff

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i know you had a rough morning. i'll hand it to carlos to give the SE read first and then we can go into timeline.
[00:17] Carlos (SE): yeah thanks maya, hi tom, lin, amira. quick tl;dr — at ~11:47 PST we saw a sudden qps spike from a batch of upstream jobs, our autoscaler triggered, but the request router started dropping or throttling sessions after the kv cache miss rate jumped. net effect was 15 to 20% elevated errors for about 40 minutes.
[00:36] Tom (BlueMarble): right, and to be clear — these were user-facing requests, not internal, it hit our shipments UI. some requests got a 503, some got a timeout. it felt nondeterministic.
[00:50] Lin (SRE): i have timeline and graphs, i'll upload them; one thing is the sequence lengths spiked because a change in our summarization prompt added history which increased tokens per request. there was also a background job that replayed older conversations around 11:40 which probably created the burst.
[01:11] Amira (Product): yes we shipped a small prompt tweak last week — not sure it would do that but maybe the combination with the replay.
[01:25] Carlos: couple of points — first the K V cache (sometimes transcribed here as K V cash) is sensitive to prefix shapes; if the replay used different prefixes the cache hit rate drops and per-token compute jumps. second the router has a short queued request budget that gets exhausted under bursts which forces the throttle.
[01:47] Maya: quick check — are you running a hosted plan with us or Dedicated?
[01:52] Tom: hosted currently. we're evaluating dedicated but wanted to understand if config changes could avoid the expense.
[02:05] Priya (CSM): thanks for clarifying, we'll try to give a cost vs benefit estimate for dedicated vs config changes.
[02:14] Lin: we also saw that some pods entered a high memory GC cycle, possibly due to larger attention caches with the longer contexts, so latency ballooned and the router thought they were unhealthy and started draining.
[02:33] Carlos: exactly — so there's a multi-factor story: cache coldness -> higher per-token compute -> memory pressure -> GC -> increased latency -> router drain -> drops.
[02:48] Tom: what's your recommended immediate mitigation? we have users right now.
[02:53] Carlos: short-term, push a fallback to a smaller model variant for requests > X tokens or when router queue depth exceeds threshold. another immediate is to enable prefix-warmers for the top 50 prefixes from your replay.
[03:13] Lin: how quickly could prefix warmers be turned on? we want something that doesn't require a deploy.
[03:18] Maya: we can toggle warmers from console today — it's a config. carlos can provide exact steps.
[03:24] Carlos: yes i'll paste steps after the call. also i want to note that the warmers only help if the traffic shape repeats — they don't help novel prefixes.
[03:36] Amira: so if we do warmers plus fallback to a smaller model we avoid dedicated?
[03:42] Carlos: maybe for now; but if your baseline sustained QPS is near our bursting threshold and you need headroom for spikes, Dedicated reduces noisy neighbor effects and gives predictable throughput. it is a cost tradeoff.
[03:58] Tom: okay let's talk costs later. i'd like a clear test to decide. what logs do you need?
[04:04] Carlos: pod-level flamegraphs, KV cache miss rates by prefix, router queue depth and reject counts, model context length distribution, and GC pause metrics. also a traffic replay so we can run benches.
[04:20] Tom: we'll give you the replay, how big should it be? single day?
[04:25] Carlos: 1–2 days around the incident is ideal. include the peak windows.
[04:31] Lin: we can package that and S3 it.
[04:35] Priya: i'll create the escalation ticket and include the S3 link and the bench window.
[04:40] Maya: good. next, medium-term — we recommend a controlled bench where we run the replay against (a) your current hosted config, (b) hosted with prefix warmers and fallback, (c) a Dedicated small pool with same model. compare error rates, p95/p99 latencies, and overall cost.
[04:59] Amira: what's the expected timeline for that bench?
[05:03] Carlos: depends on schedule but technically a couple hours to run tests plus data collation; planning and provisioning might take a day. we'd like your SRE on the call.
[05:16] Lin: we can be available next Tuesday or Wednesday.
[05:20] Maya: we'll propose Wed 2027-03-23 10:00 UTC — does that work?
[05:26] Tom: works for us.
[05:28] Amira: quick question — you mentioned throttle smoothing and gradual backoff earlier, would that prevent the drops without changing models?
[05:36] Carlos: smoothing helps reduce sudden router saturation: e.g., enforce a leaky-bucket on ingress and increase per-client soft limits. it trades a little latency for fewer rejects. it's lower cost than Dedicated but may still not cover sustained spikes.
[05:49] Lin: we also want to understand the root cause of GC — can you correlate model memory patterns with sequence length?
[05:55] Carlos: yes, that correlation is straightforward in the flamegraphs; i'll map allocs to sequence length buckets.
[06:02] Priya: i'll note that in the action items.
[06:06] Tom: there's also a compliance question — do you persist any PII in logs we'll share? we need assurance before uploading.
[06:14] Maya: good point; Redwoods' hosted logs are redacted by default and we have a process to ingest customer-supplied logs in a secure S3 bucket. we'll provide an upload guide with steps to mask PII and an NDA note if needed.
[06:29] Amira: we will mask client IDs but keep anonymized request IDs for tracing.
[06:34] Maya: perfect. follow the checklist we'll send.
[06:38] Carlos: another note — there was a model-level quantization variant we could try; it reduces memory footprint at slight quality cost. for user-facing shipments UI i'd be cautious but it's an option for background processing.
[06:52] Lin: could quantization cause regressions for our summarization accuracy?
[06:56] Carlos: small chance; we can run evaluation on a sample of the replay to measure rouge/accuracy delta.
[07:05] Tom: can you also run the bench with a rolled-back prompt so we know if the prompt tweak amplified the issue?
[07:11] Carlos: yes include scenario A (live prompt) and scenario B (previous prompt) in the replay.
[07:17] Amira: are there any quick wins to implement today?
[07:20] Maya: toggle warmers, increase router queue threshold by a small percent, and enable soft throttling smoothing — all three are low-risk config changes.
[07:30] Lin: we'll accept that as a short-term mitigation and monitor.
[07:34] Priya: i'll capture everything in the ticket and assign owners.
[07:38] Maya: anything else?
[07:40] Tom: i want to understand the cost ballpark for Dedicated — rough monthly for 4-GPU pool?
[07:47] Maya: i'll share the dedicated sizing sheet; rough ballpark will be in the doc but exact depends on model size and desired buffer. i'll put a draft to you by 2027-03-20.
[07:57] Amira: ok good.
[07:59] Carlos: final technical ask — please include a short list of 100 top prefixes by traffic in the replay so warmers can be targeted.
[08:09] Lin: we can export that.
[08:11] Maya: great. let's recap next steps — carlos will pull logs and flamegraphs, tom will upload replay (1–2 days), maya will send cost sheet and plan, priya will create ticket and schedule bench. we'll meet for the bench on 2027-03-23.
[08:31] Tom: thanks all. appreciate the quick turnaround.
[08:34] Maya: thanks everyone — we know it's urgent and we'll prioritize.
[08:38] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-attribution and word swap (e.g., KV cache -> K V cash, GC pauses sometimes transcribed as G C pauses). timestamps approximate and inserted every ~15–60s per fireflies style.
